title: Cocktails & spirits
blurb: The classic drinks people order by name, what goes in them, and the spirits behind them.

groups.name: Classic cocktails
groups.intro: The drinks every good bartender knows by name. Order one confidently and you'll sound like a regular.

items.name: Martini
items.what: Gin and dry vermouth, stirred very cold and served in a V-shaped glass with an olive or lemon twist. 'Dirty' adds olive brine.

items.name: Negroni
items.what: Bitter, ruby-red Italian aperitivo of equal parts, served over ice with orange peel.

items.name: Old Fashioned
items.what: Whisky lightly sweetened with sugar and bitters, over one big ice cube.

items.name: Manhattan
items.what: Whisky and sweet vermouth, served 'up' (no ice) with a cherry.

items.name: Margarita
items.what: Tequila, lime and orange liqueur in a salt-rimmed glass, shaken or frozen.

items.name: Mojito
items.what: Cuban highball with fresh mint and lime, topped with soda.

items.name: Daiquiri
items.what: Simple Cuban classic of rum, lime and sugar, shaken and served up.

items.name: Espresso Martini
items.what: Vodka and fresh espresso shaken to a creamy foam, topped with three coffee beans.

items.name: Aperol Spritz
items.what: Bright orange Italian aperitivo topped up with prosecco, the drink of summer terraces.

items.name: Mai Tai
items.what: Tiki-bar classic of rum, lime and almond syrup, garnished with mint.

items.name: Piña Colada
items.what: Creamy tropical blend from Puerto Rico.

items.name: Moscow Mule
items.what: Vodka and spicy ginger beer, served in a copper mug.

items.name: Whisky Sour
items.what: Whisky, lemon and sugar, often with a frothy egg-white top.

items.name: Cosmopolitan
items.what: Pink 1990s icon made famous by Sex and the City.

items.name: Bloody Mary
items.what: Savoury brunch drink of vodka and spiced tomato juice with a celery stick.

items.name: Gin and tonic
items.what: The highball everyone knows, with lime or cucumber.

items.name: Japanese highball
items.what: Japanese whisky and soda in a tall, ice-cold glass; huge in Japanese izakayas.

items.name: French 75
items.what: Gin, lemon and sugar topped with champagne, served in a flute.

items.name: Paloma
items.what: Mexico's favourite tequila drink, with grapefruit soda and a salt rim.

items.name: Caipirinha
items.what: Brazil's national cocktail: cachaça muddled with lime and sugar.

groups.name: Spirits & sparkling wine
groups.intro: The base spirits and wines behind the bar, and the words on the label.

items.name: Gin
items.what: Clear spirit flavoured with juniper; London Dry is the classic style, Japan's Roku and Hong Kong's own craft gins are popular.

items.name: Vodka
items.what: Neutral clear spirit, made from grain or potatoes.

items.name: Rum
items.what: Spirit from sugar cane or molasses: white, gold, dark or spiced.

items.name: Tequila
items.what: Mexican spirit from blue agave; blanco (unaged), reposado and añejo (aged).

items.name: Mezcal
items.what: Smoky agave spirit, mostly from Oaxaca.

items.name: Scotch whisky
items.what: Whisky made in Scotland and aged at least three years; single malt or blended.

items.name: Bourbon
items.what: American whiskey of at least 51% corn, aged in new charred oak barrels.

items.name: Japanese whisky
items.what: Scotch-style whisky; Yamazaki, Hibiki and Nikka are the names collectors chase.

items.name: Cognac
items.what: Grape brandy from the Cognac region of France, graded VS, VSOP and XO; a Hong Kong banquet favourite.

items.name: Baijiu
items.what: China's fiery, fragrant grain spirit; Kweichow Moutai is the prestige bottle at business dinners.

items.name: Sake
items.what: Japanese brewed rice drink, graded by how much the rice is polished: junmai, ginjo, daiginjo.

items.name: Soju
items.what: Korea's clear, light spirit, drunk in shots with Korean BBQ; the world's best-selling liquor brand is Jinro.

items.name: Champagne
items.what: Sparkling wine that can only come from the Champagne region of France.

items.name: Prosecco
items.what: Light, fruity Italian sparkling wine, cheaper and sweeter than champagne.
